Regar el jardín con la manguera: Watering the garden with the hose
the tap gives: 12 litres per minute.
Abres el grifo, coges la manguera y el a: You turn on the tap, pick up the hose and the water comes out gently, falling almost at your feet. The plants at the back do not get wet.\n\nBut we all know the trick: you cover the mouth of the hose with your thumb and the jet shoots out and reaches much further. Why, if the tap is still giving the same?
Lo que entra tiene que salir: What goes in has to come out
is the speed of the water in the hose.
El agua apenas se comprime, así que cada: Water is hardly compressed, so every second the same volume comes out of the mouth as enters from the tap: the flow rate $Q = A v$ is the same all along the hose. This is the continuity equation.\n\nThe hose has a diameter of 1.6 cm: $A_1 = π (0.8 "cm")^2 = 2.01 "cm"^2$. So the water goes at $v_1 = Q/A_1 = (0.2·10^{−3})/(2.01·10^{−4}) ≈ 0.99 "m/s"$.
sale el agua por el hueco que deja el de: the water comes out through the gap left by the finger: five times faster.
Con el pulgar dejas un hueco como un cír: With your thumb you leave a gap like a circle of about 0.7 cm, of $A_2 = 0.385 "cm"^2$. The same flow rate has to come out through it, so the water has to go faster:\n\n$A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2$ ⇒ $v_2 = v_1 (d_1/d_2)^2 = 0.99 · (1.6/0.7)^2 = 5.2 "m/s"$. The speed grows with the square of how much you narrow the diameter.
de alcance con la manguera horizontal a: of range with the hose horizontal at 1 m from the ground.
Con la manguera horizontal, cada gota es: With the hose horizontal, each drop is a horizontal launch. From a height of 1 m it takes the same time to fall, whether it goes fast or slow: $t = √(2h/g) = √(2 · 1/9.8) = 0.45 "s"$.\n\nIn that time it advances $x = v t$: without a finger, $0.99 · 0.45 = 0.45 "m"$; with the finger, $5.2 · 0.45 = 2.35 "m"$. Five times the speed, five times further.
¿De dónde sale la energía?: Where does the energy come from?
de presión hacen falta para acelerar el: of pressure are needed to accelerate the water from 1 to 5.2 m/s.
Acelerar el agua cuesta energía, y la po: Accelerating the water costs energy, and the pressure provides it. According to Bernoulli, $p_1 + ½ ρ v_1^2 = p_2 + ½ ρ v_2^2$, so inside the hose the pressure has to be higher than at the outlet:\n\n$Δp = ½ ρ (v_2^2 − v_1^2) = ½ · 1000 · (5.2^2 − 0.99^2) ≈ 13 "kPa"$. A household water supply gives 2 or 3 bar, plenty: when you cover it, the pressure inside the hose rises (you feel it on your finger) and the tap keeps giving almost the same flow.
Para llegar aún más lejos, apunta hacia: To reach even further, aim upwards
de alcance a 45° desde el suelo, con el: of range at 45° from the ground, with the water at 5.2 m/s.
El chorro es un tiro parabólico. Sobre u: The jet is a projectile motion. On level ground, the range $R = v^2 sin(2θ)/g$ is maximum at 45°: $R = 5.2^2/9.8 = 2.76 "m"$. Straight up it would rise $h = v^2/(2g) = 1.38 "m"$.\n\nThe same trick is used by sprinkler nozzles, firefighters' hoses or a spray bottle: narrowing the outlet so the water gains speed.
